title: The kernel-weighted radial derivative integral equals -sigma times the Laplacian paired with the potential
statement: Let n in N, rho, Psi, h : R^n -> R, x0 in R^n and sigma in R with sigma != 0. Assume h is C^2, Psi is C^1, Psi(z) = 0 whenever |z| >= 1, and DPsi(z)[v] = rho(z) <z, v> for all z, v in R^n. Then int_{R^n} rho(z) Dh(x0 + sigma z)[z] dz = - sigma int_{R^n} Laplacian(h)(x0 + sigma z) Psi(z) dz. Here Df(y)[v] = fderiv R f y v, Laplacian is Mathlib's Laplacian.laplacian, and the measure is Lebesgue measure.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (ρ Ψ h : Rn n → ℝ) (x₀ : Rn n) (σ : ℝ), σ ≠ 0 → ContDiff ℝ 2 h → ContDiff ℝ 1 Ψ → (∀ z : Rn n, 1 ≤ ‖z‖ → Ψ z = 0) → (∀ z v : Rn n, fderiv ℝ Ψ z v = ρ z * inner ℝ z v) → ∫ z, ρ z * fderiv ℝ h (x₀ + σ • z) z = -σ * ∫ z, Laplacian.laplacian h (x₀ + σ • z) * Ψ z
